drhp.business: Indosolar manufactures high-efficiency solar photovoltaic modules, with a product portfolio spanning TOPCon and Mono PERC technology, from a single facility at Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh with installed module manufacturing capacity of 1.3 GW per annum. The facility runs multiple automated production lines with stringing, layup, lamination, framing and testing equipment. As a subsidiary of Waaree Energies Limited, the Company sells modules and renders job-work services to its holding company and is also securing orders from developers of power projects.

risks.note: Escalating raw material costs could weigh on solar photovoltaic products and affect future prospects; prices of key inputs such as polysilicon, aluminium and copper have been volatile. The Company relies on pass-through clauses embedded in most orders and order-backed procurement to pass increases on to customers.
Intensifying competition presents a material risk to profitability; the Company counters with product certifications, a wide channel network, service capabilities and a low production-cost position.

Liquidity can be hit by sudden shifts in demand or pricing, or by reliance on short-term financing. Mitigated by cash and cash equivalents, expected cash accruals over the next two fiscal years, and customer advances against orders.

An extended working capital cycle could increase borrowing needs to meet operational requirements; being addressed through tighter inventory management, improved receivables collection and evaluation of factoring or supply chain financing.

Changes in government policies and regulations affecting renewable energy, including subsidies, tax incentives or import/export restrictions, could affect demand for solar products and the Company's ability to grow its market presence.

Access to skilled employees and reliable contractors is essential to maintaining operational efficiency and executing supply orders smoothly; addressed via structured training programmes and long-standing contractor/supplier ties.
risks.risk: Skilled labour and contractor availability risk

risks.note: The fast pace of advancement in solar cell efficiency and module design means manufacturers must continually innovate to stay competitive; demand is shifting toward higher-efficiency formats such as bifacial and perovskite.

The Company was not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee during FY2025-26; risk oversight rests with the Directors, with the Audit Committee having additional oversight of financial risks and controls.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
